name: PointAtMe
summary: For labelling objects in VR point clouds, a transparent box is held between the two controllers: its corners follow the controllers and its orientation follows the right controller, and a button labels the points inside.
howItWorks: The box has 9 degrees of freedom: position and size come from anchors on both virtual controllers, and orientation from the right controller only, shown by a set of axes on it. The user fits the box to an object, such as a car or cyclist in a driving scene, and confirms; camera images are shown alongside the cloud. Compared with a baseline from the literature (control-point selection by Monica et al.), labelling took about half the time per object with fewer undo actions.
advantages: About twice as fast per object as the baseline.
limitations: The comparison used different scenes from the baseline's study.

relationships.note: Two-handed box, but its orientation follows one controller instead of both hands.
